Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Daiktas, kurį duodame draugui per gimtadienį.
To say yes when another person asks for: A thing that we give to a friend on a birthday.
The child got a beautiful gift.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Rašome jį ant popieriaus ir siunčiame draugui.
To say yes when another person asks for: We write it on paper and send it to a friend.
I got a long letter from the brother.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Vieta, iš kurios siunčiame laiškus ir siuntinius.
To say yes when another person asks for: A place from which we send letters and parcels.
In the morning I go to the post office.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Gražus popierius su nuotrauka, kurį siunčiame draugams.
To say yes when another person asks for: A beautiful paper with a photograph, which we send to friends.
Grandmother got a postcard from the grandson.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Popierius, į kurį dedame laišką.
To say yes when another person asks for: A paper into which we put a letter.
The letter is in a white envelope.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Plonas baltas lapas, ant kurio rašome.
To say yes when another person asks for: A thin white sheet on which we write.
On the paper I write a letter.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Per paštą duoti laišką kitam žmogui.
To say yes when another person asks for: Through the post to give a letter to another person.
The sister sends a letter to a friend.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Imti tai, ką kitas žmogus duoda.
To say yes when another person asks for: To take what another person gives.
Yesterday I got a letter from a friend.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Visi šalies ministrai ir jų vadovas.
To say yes when another person asks for: All the country's ministers and their leader.
In the new government there are many ministers.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmonės, kuriuos renka tauta; jie daro įstatymus.
To say yes when another person asks for: People whom the nation elects; they make the laws.
In parliament work many politicians.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Lietuvos parlamentas; ten dirba šalies politikai.
To say yes when another person asks for: The parliament of Lithuania; there work the country's politicians.
Politikai Seime kalba apie naujus įstatymus.
The politicians in the Seimas talk about new laws.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Šalies vadovas; jį renka visi žmonės.
To say yes when another person asks for: The country's leader; all the people elect him.
The children saw the president on television.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Vyriausybės narys, kuris dirba su mokyklomis ar ligoninėmis.
To say yes when another person asks for: A member of the government who works with schools or hospitals.
We talked with a new minister.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Vieta mieste, kur dirba meras ir tarnautojai.
To say yes when another person asks for: A place in the city where the mayor and officials work.
The mayor works in the municipality.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Miesto vadovas; jį renka miesto žmonės.
To say yes when another person asks for: The leader of the city; the city people elect him.
People voted for a new mayor.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Maža savivaldybės dalis su kaimais.
To say yes when another person asks for: A small part of the municipality with villages.
Our village is in a big eldership.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Balsuoti už žmogų, kuris bus meras ar prezidentas.
To say yes when another person asks for: To vote for a person who will be mayor or president.
People elect a new president.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Diena, kai visi balsuoja už kandidatus.
To say yes when another person asks for: The day when everyone votes for the candidates.
After the elections there will be a new government.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Per rinkimus parodyti, kuris kandidatas tau patinka.
To say yes when another person asks for: In the elections to show which candidate you like.
My parents already voted.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, už kurį galime balsuoti per rinkimus.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person for whom we can vote in the elections.
We voted for a young candidate.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Kai kalbame apie vyriausybę, rinkimus ir įstatymus.
To say yes when another person asks for: When we talk about the government, elections and laws.
He knows much about politics.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris dirba Seime ar vyriausybėje.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who works in the Seimas or the government.
With the politician talked a journalist.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmonių grupė, kuri nori laimėti rinkimus.
To say yes when another person asks for: A group of people that wants to win the elections.
She works in a new party.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Imti parduotuvėje daiktą ir nesumokėti.
To say yes when another person asks for: To take a thing in a shop and not pay.
Someone steals bicycles in the city.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Blogas žmogus, kuris ima ne savo daiktus.
To say yes when another person asks for: A bad person who takes things that are not his own.
The police look for the thief.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Padaryti, kad kitas žmogus mirtų.
To say yes when another person asks for: To make another person die.
During the war soldiers kill people.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Daryti kitam žmogui skausmą ranka ar koja.
To say yes when another person asks for: To cause another person pain with the hand or the foot.
The angry man beat another person.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Su ginklu daryti žaizdą žmogui ar gyvūnui.
To say yes when another person asks for: With a weapon to make a wound in a person or an animal.
The soldier shot into the air.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Pavojingas daiktas, kurį kareiviai neša į karą.
To say yes when another person asks for: A dangerous thing that soldiers carry to war.
The policeman always has a weapon.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Kai blogi žmonės daro sprogimus ir žudo žmones.
To say yes when another person asks for: When bad people make explosions and kill people.
Everyone fears terrorism.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Blogos medžiagos; nuo jų žmogus serga ir miršta.
To say yes when another person asks for: Bad substances; from them a person gets sick and dies.
The police found drugs.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Jį geria bare; jis labai blogas sveikatai.
To say yes when another person asks for: They drink it in a bar; it is very bad for health.
The driver cannot drink alcohol.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris ieško vagių ir tikrina vairuotojus.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who looks for thieves and checks drivers.
Mom phoned the policeman.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Vieta, kur klausia liudininkų ir kalba advokatai.
To say yes when another person asks for: A place where they question witnesses and lawyers speak.
The thief stands in the court.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris pagal įstatymus siunčia vagį į kalėjimą.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who according to the laws sends a thief to prison.
The lawyer talks with the judge.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris teisme padeda kitam žmogui.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who in court helps another person.
He needs a good lawyer.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris teisme kalba prieš blogą žmogų.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who in court speaks against a bad person.
The judge asked the prosecutor.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris tikrina dokumentus ir sutartis.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who checks documents and contracts.
We show the documents to the notary.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Namas, kur uždaro blogus žmones.
To say yes when another person asks for: A house where they lock up bad people.
The thief sits in prison.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Tai, ko turi laikytis visi šalies žmonės.
To say yes when another person asks for: That which all the people of the country must follow.
The Seimas passed a new law.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus, kuris teisme pasakoja, ką matė.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person who in court tells what he saw.
The policeman talked with the witness.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Teisme sakyti tiesą apie tai, ką matei.
To say yes when another person asks for: In court to tell the truth about what you saw.
She testified in court.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Kai šalys nekariauja ir žmonės gyvena ramiai.
To say yes when another person asks for: When countries do not make war and people live peacefully.
Everyone wants to live in peace.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Kai šalys su ginklais žudo viena kitą.
To say yes when another person asks for: When countries with weapons kill one another.
People fear a new war.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Kai žmonės ar šalys ilgai nesutinka.
To say yes when another person asks for: When people or countries do not agree for a long time.
We talked about the conflict at work.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Visi šalies kareiviai kartu; jie turi ginklus.
To say yes when another person asks for: All the country's soldiers together; they have weapons.
The son serves in the army.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Žmogus su ginklu; jis tarnauja kariuomenėje.
To say yes when another person asks for: A person with a weapon; they serve in the army.
By the bridge stand soldiers.

Sakyti taip, kai kitas žmogus ko nors pr: Kareivių vadovas; jo klauso visi kareiviai.
To say yes when another person asks for: The soldiers' leader; all the soldiers obey him.
The soldiers listened to the officer.
